neighbours.label: the verb/noun 'remove' (removing, removed, removal): taking something away or out
fire: The crew spent the morning removing old carpet from the upstairs bedrooms.
She coordinated the removal of the paintings before the museum was renovated.
Volunteers removed tons of trash from the beach after the storm.
The dentist recommended removing the wisdom tooth before it caused problems.
The city approved the removal of the statue from the town square.
He worked for hours removing weeds from the vegetable garden.
Workers carefully removed the asbestos tiles from the school basement.
The editor asked me to remove two paragraphs from the article.
quiet: The crew spent the morning installing new carpet in the upstairs bedrooms.
She coordinated the cataloguing of the paintings before the museum was renovated.
Volunteers counted the birds on the beach after the storm.
The dentist recommended cleaning the wisdom tooth more carefully every night.
The city approved the restoration of the statue in the town square.
He worked for hours watering the plants in the vegetable garden.
Workers carefully painted the walls of the school basement.
The editor asked me to add two paragraphs to the article.

notes: Top 32: ' removing' x4, ' remove' x4, ' removal' x2, ' removed'. Note the - pole also has ' remove' in cooking 'remove from the heat' (the - pole is moving away/back); fire sentences use remove as clearing/taking out, not 'remove from heat'. Near misses keep the scene but use other verbs.
